messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for release/2026.03 -> service/inference-api in eu-west-1 (canary=10%)

samir: seeing lots of 503/429 spikes hitting inference-api-canary in eu-west. Alert: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/alerts/inference-errors - CPU looks fine but pod restarts climbing

jen: i'm oncall, taking this. samir can you paste a pod name and a quick `kubectl describe` / logs?

infra-sre: grabbing logs now. one pod: inference-api-canary-7f9d4c6ff-2lm9p
infra-sre: kubectl get pods shows CrashLoopBackOff for 4/10 canary pods
infra-sre: `kubectl logs inference-api-canary-7f9d4c6ff-2lm9p -c app` -> OOMKilled in the sidecar init sequence, then kubelet restarts

maria: fyi i reviewed the manifest in the rollout: there was a new annotation added by the feature-flag patch: `sidecar.injector.redwood/enabled: "true"` and a sidecar template change that bumps the sidecar memory to 1.5Gi in canary. I think the sidecar injection logic isn't honoring node allocatable for small instance types. diff:
```
- annotations: {}
+ annotations:
+   sidecar.injector.redwood/enabled: "true"
```
and sidecar block: `resources.requests.memory: "200Mi"` -> "1500Mi"

samir: that matches timing — feature flag `enable-new-sidecar` was flipped ~3m before the errors started. https://flags.redwood.example/flags/enable-new-sidecar

jen: ok that's actionable. i'm going to abort the feature flag (kill-switch) and scale the canary down to reduce customer impact.

jen: `ffctl toggle enable-new-sidecar --env=prod --off --reason "canary sidecar OOMs"`

deploy-bot: Feature flag change recorded: enable-new-sidecar -> OFF by jen at 1745009930 :white_check_mark:

infra-sre: also doing emergency scale: `kubectl scale deployment/inference-api-canary -n prod --replicas=0` to stop churn while flag propagates

infra-sre: patching live deployment to remove annotation as backup: `kubectl patch deployment inference-api --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/metadata/annotations/sidecar.injector.redwood~1enabled"}]'`

samir: CS reports error rate dropped by ~80% within 6 minutes after flag off. Still seeing a couple restart cycles for pods that had OOMKilled earlier.

customer-support-bot: Customer-impact: 12 customers reported increased latencies / 429s (mostly EU accounts). CS ticket #INC-5421 opened, email blast queued for affected customers.

maria: preliminary root cause: sidecar memory bump + injector logic mismatch caused sidecar to request more than node allocatable; combined with HPA scaling behavior we ended up with insufficient nodes for canary, kube evicted pods and restart loop. Also the canary manifest didn't include a safe `minReadySeconds` nor a reduced canary weight.

jen: handing off to infra-sre for remediation and post-incident follow-up. i'm marking this as mitigated in pager duty and adding notes.

infra-sre: next steps I will create a rollback PR for the injector template, add validation in the rollout job to reject sidecar mem > node allocatable, and increase HPA `minReplicas` for inference-api to 2 in eu-west.

infra-sre: creating follow-up ticket: RDW-OPS-1897 (rollback injector template + rollout job validation + canary safety checks) link: https://issues.redwood.example/RDW-OPS-1897

jen: nice work. please include a postmortem doc and add a test that simulates small-node allocations. cc @maria for the injector changes.

samir: can we also add an alert rule to catch sudden pod OOM spikes per deployment? that would have paged earlier.

maria: yes adding rule to the infra alerts board now.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout halted for release/2026.03 in eu-west-1 by jen (kill-switch).

jen: closing the incident channel for now, leaving follow-ups in RDW-OPS-1897. if anything pops back up i'll reopen. :thumbsup:
